docs.title: Search and Retrieval
docs.text:
ChatVault AI has two different search experiences:

Experience Where What it searches Library title search Library page Conversation titles in the loaded list, in the browser Semantic search POST /api/v1/search Embedded chunks in ChromaDB, validated against SQLite

There is no dedicated semantic search screen in the current frontend. Use AI Chat for an answer, or call the search endpoint directly for ranked chunks.

docs.title: Semantic search API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "reset the Shell-GPT API key",
    "limit": 5
  }'

Request fields:

Field Type Required Constraints Meaning query string Yes 1-2000 characters after trimming, not blank Text to embed and search limit integer No 1-20, default 5 Maximum results after filtering conversation_id string or null No Existing conversation ID Restrict retrieval to one conversation

Example response:

{
  "query": "reset the Shell-GPT API key",
  "total": 2,
  "results": [
    {
      "conversation_id": "abc123",
      "conversation_title": "Shell-GPT setup notes",
      "role": "user",
      "message_position": 4,
      "chunk_index": 0,
      "text": "How do I reset the Shell-GPT API key?",
      "distance": 0.1823
    },
    {
      "conversation_id": "def456",
      "conversation_title": "API key rotation",
      "role": "assistant",
      "message_position": 7,
      "chunk_index": 1,
      "text": "Remove the saved key and run sgpt --api-key again.",
      "distance": 0.2417
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: How retrieval works
docs.text:
1. The query is trimmed and validated.
  2. The embedding model is checked against the collection provenance.
  3. The query is embedded with OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL.
  4. ChromaDB is queried with cosine distance.
  5. The backend requests max(limit * 4, limit) candidates.
  6. Candidate conversation IDs are validated against SQLite.
  7. Orphaned vectors whose SQLite conversation was deleted are discarded.
  8. Results are returned up to limit.

Step 5 is deliberate: if ChromaDB contains stale vectors, over-fetching prevents them from consuming the caller's result budget.

docs.title: Distance, not similarity
docs.text:
distance is the raw cosine distance returned by ChromaDB. Lower is closer. It is not converted to a percentage and no similarity threshold is applied. A result can be returned even when it is only weakly related.

There is no hybrid keyword search, BM25, reranker, or score normalization. The ranking is the collection's cosine ranking after orphan filtering.

docs.title: Restrict to one conversation
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "Docker compose volume",
    "limit": 3,
    "conversation_id": "abc123"
  }'

The where filter is applied inside ChromaDB. Results are still validated against SQLite.

docs.title: Requirements and errors
docs.text:
Semantic search requires:

  • Ollama running and reachable.
  • OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL installed.
  • A compatible ChromaDB collection.
  • At least one indexed conversation for non-empty results.
Status Meaning 200 Search completed; total may be zero 422 Blank query, value out of range, or invalid request 503 Ollama or ChromaDB unavailable, or the embedding model is missing 502 Ollama returned an invalid embedding response 409 Collection provenance or distance configuration is incompatible 500 ChromaDB query failed

An empty collection returns 200 with "total": 0, not an error.

docs.title: Library title search
docs.text: The Library search box filters the loaded set of up to 100 conversations by title. It does not query the backend and does not use embeddings. See Library Management.

docs.title: Practical tips
docs.text:
• Use natural-language phrases that resemble the stored text.
  • Restrict to one conversation when you know where the answer lives.
  • If results are poor, verify the conversation is indexed and the index is not stale.
  • If the embedding model changed, rebuild the index before searching.
  • Inspect distance values to judge how close the matches are, but do not treat them as calibrated confidence.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings at /settings is an operational status page, not a configuration editor. It reads the current environment, Ollama state, ChromaDB state, and SQLite counts. The only mutation is a full vector index rebuild.

docs.title: Ollama connection
docs.text:
Shows:

  • Configured OLLAMA_BASE_URL.
  • Whether the /api/tags request succeeded.
  • Number of installed models.
  • Time of the last status read.

If Ollama is unavailable, the panel displays a public error message and suggests starting the service with ollama serve.

docs.title: Configured models
docs.text:
Shows the chat and embedding model names selected by the backend environment and whether each is installed.

Model matching treats an unversioned name as matching its latest tag. For example, configured llama3.2:3b matches installed llama3.2:3b; a configured name without a tag also matches an installed name:tag.

If a model is missing, pull it:

ollama pull llama3.2:3b
ollama pull nomic-embed-text

docs.title: ChromaDB vector store
docs.text:
Shows the collection name, live vector count, embedding dimension, and availability. If the store cannot be read, the error is shown.

Deleting storage/chroma/ or rebuilding the index does not delete conversations. SQLite remains the source of truth.

docs.title: SQLite database
docs.text: Shows the engine (sqlite), conversation count, message count, and indexed chunk count. The panel notes that message text is stored locally and that application logs do not include conversation snippets.

docs.title: Indexing
docs.text:
Shows:

  • Coverage percentage (indexed / total).
  • Indexed, not indexed, failed, and stale counts.
  • Chunk size, overlap, minimum, chunking version, token-counting method, and embedding dimension.
  • Rebuild-required state and reason.
  • The last rebuild result, if one was run in this session.

Chunking values are read from GET /api/v1/index/status. The summary above them comes from GET /api/v1/models/status.

docs.title: Installed Ollama models
docs.text: Lists every model reported by Ollama with size, modification date, and badges showing whether it is the configured chat model or embedding model.

docs.title: Rebuild the index
docs.text:
Rebuild index opens a confirmation dialog. Confirming calls:

POST /api/v1/index/rebuild

The operation:

  1. Verifies the embedding model is available.
  2. Deletes and recreates the ChromaDB collection.
  3. Resets every conversation's index state to not_indexed.
  4. Re-chunks and re-embeds every conversation.
  5. Returns a summary with indexed, skipped, and failed counts.

SQLite conversations and messages are not modified. The request is synchronous and can take minutes on a large library. The UI stays in a loading state until it finishes.

Use a rebuild when:

  • The embedding model changed.
  • The embedding dimension changed.
  • The collection has unknown provenance.
  • The collection is empty but conversations are marked indexed.
  • The chunking configuration changed and you want a full refresh.

Individual stale conversations can also be reindexed with POST /api/v1/index/{conversation_id}; the UI does not expose a per-conversation reindex action outside the Import retry flow.

docs.title: Refresh status
docs.text: Refresh status refetches both GET /api/v1/models/status and GET /api/v1/index/status. TanStack Query also marks the data stale after 15 seconds and refetches when the query is used again. The page does not poll on a timer.

docs.title: What Settings cannot change
docs.text:
• Environment variables or .env values.
  • Ollama base URL.
  • Model names.
  • Chunk sizes or chunking version.
  • Database or ChromaDB paths.
  • CORS origins.
  • API port or host.
  • Chat history or context limits.

Change these in the root .env, then restart the backend. See Configuration.
